THEAMERICANTOBACCCOCOMPANY	THEAMERICANTOBACCCOCOMPANY	MemorandumCONFIDENTIAL
To	Mr. R. S. Sprinkle, III	Date July 21, 1988
From	B. F. Price and D. O. Pinion	
Ref	Weekly Report - Research Section	

"Smokeless" cigarette development work is summarized as follows:

We completed puff-by-puff temperature measurements on eight of thirteen different fuel element formulations. As reported last week, technique refinement that gives more reproducible results is also showing higher temperatures. These changes will require us to return to previous work and put everything on a common base. We now see nearly a  \( 400^{\circ} \) C change, when measured directly behind the fuel element, due to fuel pellet composition. Diluents such as bone carbon and fuller's earth are effective temperature reducing agents.

Preliminary analysis of a carbon stick used in one style of hand warmer shows the presence of silicone oil, PVA and \(\mathrm{KNO}_3\). Aroma while burning suggests that lauryl alcohol is also present. Quantitative estimates will be made.

Burn regulation work is summarized below:

An order of standard cotton velvet fabric was shipped regular UPS last Friday by Momentum Textiles in California. We expect it to arrive by the end of this week.
A PALL MALL Famous model cigarette wrapped with Ecusta 04018 paper containing propenyl guaethol glucoside did not perform any differently than a control when smoldered on our three mock-ups.

Our mass burn and LOI data is fitting nicely with flux, IR thermometry and mock-up smolder values. Worst case ignitions appear to have mass burn rates near 60 mg/minute and about 10% LOI; best results are found at about 40 mg/minute and 21% LOI. A denicotinized PALL MALL Famous blend model has values close to the control: 58 mg/minute, 8% LOI and 45 kW/cm² flux.
Kimberly-Clark is just getting around to filling some of our requests for smolder-retardant-filled cigarette papers using materials we provided. The Huber sodium-aluminum-carbonate product will require a binder; a sodium stannate-filled paper is scheduled for next week.

Some publications about smoldering of cellulosics indicate modifications to the cellulosic polymer, which increase char and reduce pyrolytic formation
